chain.label: Tailwind on runway 8
chain.trigger: Runway 8 was wet, and a 6-knot tailwind existed at the time of the accident; the captain noted a 20-knot tailwind indication on the FMS during the approach

chain.label: Short wet runway with no departure-end safety area
chain.trigger: runway 8 was 6,032 feet long and did not have a 1,000-foot runway safety area... A metal blast fence is located 32 feet from the departure end of runway 8

chain.label: Controller vectored flight onto final only 8 nm from threshold
chain.trigger: Flight 1455 was given vectors that resulted in interception of the final approach course about 8 nm west of the runway threshold

chain.label: 230-knot speed restriction not cancelled before approach clearance
chain.trigger: “Southwest fourteen fifty five, maintain two thirty or greater 'til advised please”; the controller “stated that he did not know why he did not cancel the speed restriction before issuing the approach clearance”

chain.label: Captain delayed reducing airspeed and configuring the airplane
chain.trigger: the flight crew did not extend the speed brakes or flaps until about 1809, more than 1 minute after the approach clearance was issued

caused_by.evidence: Canceling the speed adjustment would have permitted the accident captain to begin to reduce his speed about 37 seconds sooner, thereby giving him more time to properly execute his approach to land
This vector put the airplane in an unfavorable position for final approach, complicated the accident flight crew's approach planning and execution

chain.label: OPC landing module not used despite tailwind, high weight, short runway
chain.trigger: The first officer did not use, and the captain did not call for the use of, the Onboard Performance Computer (OPC) landing module during the approach

chain.label: Steep, excessively fast final descent (7 degrees, 2,200 fpm, 182-200 knots)
chain.trigger: the airplane descended at an average flightpath angle of about 7 degrees until flare, at an average vertical speed of 2,200 feet per minute, and at indicated airspeeds of between 182 and 200 knots

caused_by.evidence: The captain's delay in reducing airspeed and configuring the airplane caused the flight crew to initiate final descent at a higher altitude and a faster airspeed than normal, contributing to the unstabilized approach
the actions of the SCT Woodland controller positioned the airplane too fast, too high, and too close to the runway threshold to leave any safe options other than a go-around maneuver
The captain indicated that having to keep his speed up (to 230 knots) and the tailwind contributed to the fast approach

chain.label: First officer made no airspeed, sink rate, or altitude callouts
chain.trigger: the first officer indicated that his attention was focused primarily outside the airplane and acknowledged that he did not call out airspeed or sink rate deviations to the captain

chain.label: Captain fixated on runway and disregarded GPWS sink rate and pull-up alerts
chain.trigger: he did not react to the warning because he did not feel that he had to take action; he became “fixated on the runway”

caused_by.evidence: the GPWS “sink rate” and “whoop, whoop, pull up” alerts sounded several times. The GPWS warnings should have given the flight crew a strong indication that the approach was unstabilized

if the first officer had made the airspeed and sink rate deviation callouts or altitude callouts, both the captain and the first officer might have been further alerted to the fact that the airplane's airspeed and sink rate were excessive
The OPC landing module would have provided the flight crew with useful landing information about the configuration and condition data for computation of landing distance, speeds, and power settings

chain.label: Required go-around not executed although airplane was not “in the slot”
chain.trigger: he could not explain why he did not perform a go-around maneuver

caused_by.evidence: He stated that the airport looked normal at 500 feet but that he was not “in the slot” because his airspeed was too high

the accident airplane's approach was unstabilized and not in compliance with Southwest Airlines operating procedures... because the airplane was not in the proper position to land, a go-around maneuver should have been performed

chain.label: Long, fast touchdown 2,150 feet beyond threshold at 182 knots
chain.trigger: the airplane touched down at about 182 knots, which is 44 knots over the reference speed for this flight... about 2,150 feet beyond the runway 8 threshold

caused_by.evidence: The Safety Board concludes that the flight crew landed the airplane at an excessive airspeed
Runway 8 was wet, and a 6-knot tailwind existed at the time of the accident

chain.label: Overran departure end of runway 8
chain.trigger: overran the departure end of runway 8 after landing at Burbank-Glendale-Pasadena Airport

caused_by.evidence: even if the accident flight crew had applied maximum manual brakes immediately upon touchdown, the airplane would not likely have stopped before impacting the blast fence

the accident airplane would have required about 4,700 feet of runway length after touchdown to stop using maximum manual brakes... the accident airplane traveled about 4,150 feet from touchdown to impact with the blast fence

chain.label: Collision with blast fence and airport perimeter wall
chain.trigger: at approximately 32 knots, collided with a metal blast fence and an airport perimeter wall... came to rest on a city street; the nose gear collapsed

caused_by.evidence: The airplane departed the right side of the runway about 30 degrees from the runway heading, penetrated a metal blast fence and an airport perimeter wall
no significant longitudinal RSA exists on the departure end of runway 8. A metal blast fence is located 32 feet from the departure end of runway 8

chain.label: Two serious and 42 minor injuries
chain.trigger: 2 passengers sustained serious injuries; 41 passengers and the captain sustained minor injuries

caused_by.evidence: The airplane sustained extensive exterior damage and some internal damage to the passenger cabin
